chief_complaint: intrusive germs thoughts leading to handwashing 5 hours
hpi_details: A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with intrusive germs thoughts leading to handwashing 5 hours. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks dangerous bacteria and toxic germs from outside have contaminated her house and cannot be removed with regular soap.
concerns: She is worried that missing a tiny contaminated spot will pass a lethal infection to her elderly mother.
expectations: She hopes to receive a hospital-grade antiseptic wash for her hands and something to stop the overwhelming urge to keep scrubbing.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes exposure and response prevention; a qualified prescriber may consider and monitor an SSRI, tailored to individual risk factors and severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Acute suicidal or homicidal ideation.
management_principles: Offer exposure and response prevention therapy.
A qualified prescriber may consider and monitor an SSRI, including adverse effects and emergent suicidality.
Assess suicidal or homicidal ideation and arrange urgent psychiatric evaluation if risk is imminent.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: Can you describe the thoughts about germs that keep intruding on your mind?
How many hours a day do you spend washing your hands?
Do you feel these thoughts are excessive, but you can't stop the washing?
Has this affected your work, relationships, or the skin on your hands?
Do you avoid touching things or shaking hands because of contamination fears?

history.answer: I keep having distressing thoughts that my hands are contaminated with germs, and I spend up to five hours a day washing them.
Whenever I touch any surface, sudden intrusive thoughts flood in that dangerous bacteria are crawling on my skin, which triggers intense anxiety.
I scrub my hands with antibacterial soap repeatedly throughout the day, and altogether it easily takes up four to five hours.
I realize deep down that my hands aren't truly that dirty and that this level of washing makes no sense, but the urge feels impossible to resist.
I go out of my way to avoid touching doorknobs, elevator buttons, and handrails, and I refuse to use public restrooms altogether.
My hands have become raw, cracked, and painful from all the scrubbing, and the hours spent washing leave me exhausted and unable to finish my daily chores.
The intrusive thoughts started about four months ago and have gradually worsened to the point where they consume my entire routine.
The anxiety doesn't come out of the blue as a sudden ten-minute panic attack; instead, it steadily builds up whenever I try to stop myself from washing.
I don't get sudden heart pounding, choking sensations, chest pain, dizziness, or a feeling that I'm about to die.
No, I don't feel unusually anxious about public speaking, meeting people, or being evaluated socially.
I feel drained and physically fatigued from the endless cleaning cycles, but I don't spend my day worrying about everyday matters like finances or family health.
I don't hear voices or believe anyone is intentionally trying to infect me; I know these thoughts come entirely from my own mind.
I have never experienced any traumatic life events or physical violence, and I don't have nightmares or flashbacks.
I feel overwhelmed and distressed by how much this is controlling my life, but I have never wanted to end my life and have no thoughts of hurting myself.
No, my weight has been steady, I don't feel overly hot, I'm not sweating excessively, and my hands don't shake.
I have never experienced chest tightness, shortness of breath, or fainting during exercise.
I only drink one cup of green tea in the morning, and I don't drink coffee or energy drinks.
I don't take sleeping pills or tranquilizers, and I haven't had any alcohol withdrawal or used illegal drugs.
I tried wearing gloves and forcing myself to delay washing, but the distress became unbearable until I gave in; I have never sought psychiatric help before.
I keep feeling like deadly bacteria from outside got tracked into my house, and normal soap just isn't enough to get rid of them.
I'm terrified that if my hands aren't completely clean, I'll pass a deadly bug to my elderly mother and make her gravely ill.
I was hoping for a prescription-strength skin disinfectant and some medicine to quiet these constant urges to wash.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure, diabetes, or asthma.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter remedies, or nutritional supplements.
I do not have any allergies to medications or other substances.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only have an occasional glass of wine when dining out with friends, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an office clerk and live in an apartment with my husband.
No one in my family has obsessive-compulsive disorder or any other diagnosed mental health condition.
My menstrual cycle is regular every twenty-eight days, my last period started two weeks ago, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 15 breaths per minute, and temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius.
Alert, casually dressed female who appears weary and anxious, with visibly reddened and chafed skin over both hands.

Oriented to person, place, and time, with anxious affect, spontaneous and coherent speech, preserved insight into the irrational nature of her behaviors, and no signs of psychosis or suicidal ideation.
Marked erythema, dryness, and superficial fissures across the dorsum of both hands and wrists without purulent drainage, swelling, or fluctuance.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, non-tender, with no palpable nodules or bruits.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light; extraocular movements are intact with no exophthalmos or lid lag.
Regular rhythm and rate with normal S1 and S2 sounds, and no audible murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds and no wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
No resting or postural tremor observed in either outstretched upper extremity.
